criteria.criterion: In docs/spec.toml, requirement OLY-B-NOTE-01 has a mechanism that is no longer "none" and names crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs (`specialization`) and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, both found by Grep; owner stays Athena; measure says how it is shown and ends with `status: specialization`, a heading display.rs prints.
criteria.evidence: From the diff: the mechanism now names `specialization in crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs` and `crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs`, and the owner is still "Athena". The measure ends `status: specialization`. Grep found `pub fn specialization` at planning.rs:488 and `specialization_lines` at display.rs:185. That function prints a line starting `specialization   per class of work...` (display.rs:192). `("specialization", "specialization")` is listed in STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS (status.rs:313). The measure's 'at least 3 jobs' matches SPECIALIZATION_MIN_JOBS = 3 (planning.rs:457).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: crates/athena-cli/tests/routing_evidence.rs builds fixture records where a non-baseline model/effort setting with at least SPECIALIZATION_MIN_JOBS jobs has a higher landed share, and asserts `display::status` prints the `specialization` line flagging it as helping; a second case with fewer jobs asserts no flag. Removing the figure or its display makes it fail.
criteria.evidence: I ran the new tests and all 3 passed. The first test's fixture puts 4 `medium` jobs in class code, 1 of them landed (this is the baseline), and SPECIALIZATION_MIN_JOBS (3) `high` jobs, all landed. It asserts that `display::status` contains `\nspecialization   per class` and `code: specialization helps: m · high beat the default`. The second test has 2 `high` jobs and asserts there is no `specialization helps` and that `code: not enough jobs` appears. Both tests require the `specialization   per class` header, which only specialization_lines prints. So removing the figure or its display makes both fail. I judged this from the code; I did not edit files. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` passed on this tree (CI run 43282822612).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test in routing_evidence.rs calls `display::snapshot_status` on a fixture snapshot and asserts the `specialization` block appears; it fails if the snapshot print line in display.rs or the SnapshotView field in snapshot.rs is removed.
criteria.evidence: `status_snapshot_prints_the_specialization_block_from_the_snapshot_records` passed. It writes a real snapshot with `snapshot::write` from fixture git records, then reads it back with `snapshot::status`. It calls `athena_cli::display::snapshot_status` and asserts the header, the helping flag and `m · medium: 4 jobs`. The only place snapshot_status prints this block is the new line display.rs:1232, so removing that line fails the assertions. Removing the `SnapshotView.specialization` field (snapshot.rs:247) breaks compilation of display.rs. Both conclusions come from reading the code; I made no edits.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence directory>` on the real records: the `specialization` block lists each class of work and its per-setting job counts sum to the expected range, which is the number of dispatched request jobs with a producer invocation counted from history.json and the recorded invocations (a source the change does not compute), within 0 difference. Every class flagged as helping has at least 3 jobs in that setting.
criteria.evidence: The snapshot run lists 7 classes: build, code, config, design, docs, prompts and tests. Their per-setting job counts are 5, 560, 38, 50, 58, 31 and 26, which sum to 768. For the independent count I used the evidence snapshot's invocation files, not code from the change. Grep found 868 producer invocation files: 321, 277, 64, 179 and 27 across five date ranges. In the sorted `ls` listings, 42, 30, 7, 19 and 2 job directories (100 in total) hold a second producer file. A Glob of 2026111* covered the last range. That leaves 868 − 100 = 768 unique jobs with a producer run, a difference of 0. The bootstrap job has no invocations, so no non-request job adds a producer run. Three classes are flagged as helping: code (claude-sonnet-5-5 · high, 193 jobs), prompts (claude-haiku-5-5 · unrecorded, 3 jobs) and tests (claude-sonnet-5-5 · unrecorded, 7 jobs). Each has at least 3 jobs.

summary: The change passes: all seven criteria are met and there are no blocker or major findings. OLY-B-NOTE-01 now has a mechanism: the existing `specialization` figure in planning.rs, printed by display.rs. Its measure ends with `status: specialization`, a heading that exists. The change also prints the specialization block in `athena status --snapshot`. This retry fixes the earlier gaps. I ran the three new tests in routing_evidence.rs and they pass: a setting with enough jobs is flagged as helping, one with fewer jobs is not, and the snapshot path is covered. On the real records the per-setting job counts sum to 768. I counted 768 jobs with a producer run independently from the invocation files, so the difference is 0. Every class flagged as helping has at least 3 jobs. The diff touches only listed deliverables, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. I could not run the base build for criterion 5's before/after comparison. The diff shows the change only appends a block after the throughput section, so the earlier lines cannot change. One thing to watch, not caused by this change: the existing throughput section reports a median 'landing and rebuild' time of 2098.8 min, far from the 'few minutes' the criterion expected.
